claim: When you use AWS WAF on CloudFront, your rules run in all AWS edge locations close to end users, and blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers.
question: Where do AWS WAF rules run for a CloudFront distribution?

values.display: your rules run in all AWS Edge Locations
Blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers.

evidence.quote: When you use AWS WAF on Amazon CloudFront, your rules run in all AWS Edge Locations, located around the world close to your end users. This means security doesn’t come at the expense of performance. Blocked requests are stopped before they reach your web servers.

claim: When you use AWS WAF on regional services such as Application Load Balancer, Amazon API Gateway and AWS AppSync, your rules run in the Region and can protect internet-facing resources as well as internal resources.
question: Can AWS WAF on an ALB protect an internal (not internet-facing) application?

values.display: internet-facing resources as well as internal resources

evidence.quote: When you use AWS WAF on regional services, such as Application Load Balancer, Amazon API Gateway, and AWS AppSync, your rules run in region and can be used to protect internet-facing resources as well as internal resources.

claim: You can configure Amazon Security Lake to collect web ACL data, and AWS WAF does not charge for using this option (Security Lake pricing applies).
question: Besides logging, how can AWS WAF data reach Amazon Security Lake, and does AWS WAF charge for it?

values.display: AWS WAF doesn't charge you for using this option.

evidence.quote: AWS WAF doesn't charge you for using this option.
Security Lake collects log and event data from various sources for normalization, analysis, and management.
